summary: Remote-controlled PTY and self-upgrade over WebSocket give operators full shell access to the installer host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent runs as a long-lived process that connects out to a configurable WebSocket server and dispatches server-sent messages to local handlers. One handler forwards `terminal_input` bytes directly into a spawned PTY (`term.pty.write(msg.data)`), granting whoever controls the WebSocket endpoint an interactive shell on the installer's host. Other handlers write and delete files, run git operations, and, on an `upgrade_agent` message, resolve `@yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` from the npm registry and reinstall/restart the agent under systemd/launchd/PM2 with the agent's privileges — the executed version is whatever the registry serves at that moment, not pinned or signed. Together these handlers form a full-host remote-access and persistence surface: any party controlling (or able to spoof during reconnect) the configured WebSocket server obtains RCE, file manipulation, and auto-update control on the host running the agent. The service/linux.js PATH modification installs the agent as a background service, and msal-browser.min.js contains vendor authentication code unrelated to the backdoor surface.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
